STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall or bowl shadow).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the cucumber slices are about 5-6 cm long; the plate spans roughly 4-5 of these across its width, giving about 22-27 cm. The meat pieces are about 5-7 cm long, consistent with this.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm, so area ≈ 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Cucumber (sliced, raw): covers roughly 12% of the plate, about 75 cm². Slices are thin, so average thickness about 0.8 cm (a flat layer of slices, a few stacked at one point). Volume ≈ 60 ml x 0.6 density ≈ 36 g. Take 40 g.
- Grilled/roasted meat (pork or chicken-like, several pieces, sliced): covers roughly 15% of the plate, about 95 cm². Pieces are 1-1.5 cm thick on average, with a few thicker chunks. Volume ≈ 95 x 1.2 ≈ 115 ml x 1.0 density ≈ 115 g. Take 110 g.
- Sauce or dressing: only faint traces, negligible (about 2 g).

Hidden food: no base layer visible; the plate is flat, so nothing is hidden beneath.

STEP 4 - Total ≈ 40 + 110 + 2 ≈ 152 g. This is a light portion.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Cucumber, raw: about 15 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked meat (roasted pork or chicken, mixed pieces with some fat): about 200 kcal/100 g.
- Sauce traces: about 80 kcal/100 g.

Energy: cucumber 40 g → 6 kcal; meat 110 g → 220 kcal; sauce 2 g → 2 kcal; total ≈ 228 kcal.
